case.name: Houston Ship Channel collision, Bayport Flare, Upper Galveston Bay, Texas, 2019-05-10

wind_station.name: Eagle Point, Galveston Bay, TX (NOAA CO-OPS)

current_station.name: Fred Hartman Bridge, Houston Ship Channel, TX (NOAA CO-OPS PORTS)

scene.provenance: Geometry generated by scripts/0_make_spill_observation.py: 3000 particles advected by NOAA CO-OPS observed currents (station g08010 bin 30) plus 0.025-0.035 windage on NOAA CO-OPS observed wind (station 8771013), with 2.0 m2/s eddy diffusion, from a real AIS-derived release point/time. The release, the wind and the current are real; the polygon geometry is not an observation.

wind_station.name: Eagle Point, Galveston Bay, TX (NOAA CO-OPS)

current_station.name: Fred Hartman Bridge, Houston Ship Channel, TX (NOAA CO-OPS PORTS)

environment.limitation: Single-point wind and single-point, mid-depth current, applied as spatially uniform fields. No coastline, no bathymetry, no spatial shear.

backtrack.method: Backward displacement of the slick centroid by the vector-mean of (observed current + wind_drift_factor * observed wind) over the candidate age interval. One candidate origin per candidate age; the age is not resolved by this step.
backtrack.uncertainty_model: r = max(250 m, 0.25 x backtrack distance) -- a stated heuristic, not a calibrated error model.

release.note: Midpoint of the stopped positions of VOYAGER (29.59581, -94.94310, 20:27:25Z) and ROSE BALSAM (29.60061, -94.94655, 20:26:38Z).

356144000.role: outbound ship that struck the tow; later NUC

366996020.role: towing vessel pushing the tank barge that was breached

sensitivity_no_heading.note: Reported as sensitivity only. Headline uses spec weights.

caveats: The spill polygon is SYNTHETIC (forward Lagrangian simulation). The release point/time, wind, currents and all vessel tracks are real.
Drift uses single-point observed wind and a single mid-depth current bin as spatially uniform fields. No coastline, bathymetry or shear.
The slick age is not resolved; each vessel matches its own best age.
An AIS gap is a soft positive signal only and is never treated as proof of responsibility.
No claim of production-grade accuracy. This is a feasibility test of the pipeline, not a validated attribution system.
